transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… mostly my sleep. I mean, I know everyone’s tired and work is stressful, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’m barely sleeping in a way that feels useful anymore. I lie there replaying client models in my head, and then I’ll wake up around 3 or 4 with my stomach all tight. By the time I go to work, it feels like I never really rested at all. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you tell me more about how long it takes you to fall asleep and if you wake up during the night?

It can take quite a while… I don’t usually look at the clock the whole time, but I’ll be lying there with my mind going over client models and numbers, and it just doesn’t switch off. And then even if I do fall asleep, I tend to wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach all tight. After that it’s hard to feel like I’ve really slept, so I go into work feeling like I never actually rested. Is that… the sort of detail you’re looking for?
When you’re lying awake or after you wake up in the early hours, do you find yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but yes. Most days there’s this kind of heavy, gray feeling, at work and even when I’m back at my apartment. I’m functioning, I think—I get through what I’m supposed to—but it feels like I’m just going through the motions. And sometimes if someone asks me something completely normal, I have to work not to tear up, which feels embarrassing. Is that what you mean by feeling down?
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy or felt fatigued most days, even after you rest?

I’m not sure how to separate that from just… normal work tiredness, honestly. I do feel worn out a lot, but I keep telling myself it’s because I’m not sleeping well or because the workload has been heavy. I wouldn’t want to exaggerate it.

Even if I rest, I don’t always feel refreshed, but I’m still getting myself to work and doing what I need to do. Does that answer it, or do you mean something more specific by fatigue?
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends, don’t feel as rewarding or pleasurable as they used to?

I… I’m not sure. I mean, I still do things when I’m supposed to, like if a friend asks to get coffee I’ll usually go, and I don’t want to make it sound like nothing ever feels good.

Maybe it’s just harder for me to tell lately what “enjoying” is supposed to feel like. I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear before-and-after, if that makes sense. I can say I haven’t really been paying much attention to hobbies or that kind of thing. Is that a useful answer, or do you want me to think about specific examples?
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you're not good enough, even when others might not see it that way?

I guess… yes, probably. I don’t want to sound overly dramatic, but at work, if a manager questions one of my projections, I immediately take it as proof that I’m not as sharp as I used to be. Like everyone can see I’m failing, even if they’re just asking a normal question.

I know that may not be completely rational, but that’s where my mind goes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still, especially when you're feeling down?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, I probably look a little tired sometimes, but I don’t think I’m moving unusually slowly or pacing around or anything like that.

I do sit at my desk a lot, so maybe I’m not the best judge. But no, I wouldn’t say that’s been a clear issue for me. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
How long have you been feeling this way overall—like you're going through the motions, having trouble sleeping, and feeling down?

It’s been… quite a while, I guess. I don’t want to overstate it, but probably about three years now.

It seemed to start after the merger, when our Caribbean-market division got reorganized. I kept thinking I’d adjust and it would pass, but it’s sort of just stayed in the background since then. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Have you noticed these symptoms happening even when there hasn’t been a specific stressor or when you’re not particularly worried about work or other obligations?

Yes… I think so. I wish I could say it’s only when something specific happens, like a deadline or a difficult meeting, but a lot of days it’s just there.

I’ll be walking through the office, or even just at home in my apartment, and there’s this heavy, gray feeling. Like I’m just getting through the motions and trying to keep myself together. Sometimes someone will ask me a completely normal question, and I can feel myself getting close to tears for no real reason.

I know that probably sounds like too much, but… yes, it does happen even when nothing in particular is wrong. Is that helpful?
Have you found yourself feeling excessively worried, on edge, or restless, even when there isn’t a specific problem to solve?

I’m not sure I’d describe it as excessively worried, exactly. I mean, I do think about things, probably more than I should sometimes, but I don’t feel like I’m constantly on edge with no reason.

Restless… not really. I’m usually more just trying to get through the day than feeling keyed up. But maybe I’m not separating those things very well. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came out of nowhere, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had stressful moments, of course, but not sudden attacks where my heart is racing or I can’t breathe out of nowhere.

At least, not that I would recognize as that. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think I’ve had anything dramatic like that. My appetite maybe goes up and down a little, but I haven’t really noticed losing weight without trying or eating much less in a way that stands out.

I’m sorry, I know that’s not a very precise answer. I just haven’t been tracking it closely.
Have you noticed that your mood improves at all when something good happens, like if a friend says something nice or you have a small success at work?

A little, maybe, but it doesn’t seem to last very long. Like, if someone says something nice, I can appreciate it on some level, and I don’t want to sound ungrateful… but most days there’s still this heavy, gray feeling underneath everything.

I can be at the office or even just at home in my apartment, and I’m sort of moving through things, going through the motions. Sometimes if someone asks me a normal question, I feel like I have to work not to tear up, which feels embarrassing to admit. Does that make sense?
Have you found that you no longer take pleasure in almost any activities, even things you used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or doing small things you used to find satisfying?

I’m not sure I’d say almost any activities. That sounds… very total, and I don’t want to exaggerate.

There are definitely things that don’t feel as satisfying as they probably should, but I can still sometimes enjoy parts of them, or at least appreciate them. Maybe it’s more muted than gone. Is that the kind of distinction you’re asking about?
Even aside from how tired you feel from not sleeping well, have you noticed that you have less energy than usual or feel fatigued even after resting?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that from sleep, honestly. I do feel tired a lot, but I tend to assume it’s because I didn’t sleep well or because work is just… draining.

Even when I rest, I don’t always feel refreshed, but I don’t know if I’d call it a separate “low energy” thing. Maybe it is. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say you often feel anxious or worried about things, even when there’s no clear reason or specific problem to focus on?

I don’t think so… not in a constant way, at least. I mean, I worry about the normal things—work, bills, whether I’m keeping up—but I usually can point to what it’s about.

I wouldn’t say I’m just anxious for no reason most of the time. Or… I haven’t really noticed it that way. Is that helpful, or am I answering too narrowly?
